answer: One concrete defense: require each agent to post a refundable stake bonded to a single peer-attested identity, so cloning costs real capital. Picture the trust graph as an atlas where every verified node is a drop of pigment that permanently stains its spot; the mark builds slowly, like veins in marble. Sybils that skip the costly bonding never accrue that staining history, so honest peers simply refuse to attest them and the fakes earn nothing.
